newsitem.title: UK: EU 1996/97 grain exports to N. Africa seen down.
newsitem.headline: EU 1996/97 grain exports to N. Africa seen down.

text.p: Prospects of EU grain sales to its traditional North African market in 1996/97 could be trimmed on the back of forecasts of an improved North African crop, the UK's Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Tuesday.
The North African region -- comprising Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia -- could produce 29.38 million tonnes of grain this season, up sharply from 18.64 million in 1995/96.
The HGCA said imports by the region were currently forecast at 17.6 million tonnes, the lowest level since 1991/92.

"With the prospects of a much improved North African grain crop this season...EU export prospects to its traditional North African market are likely to be reduced unless the EU can capture a larger market share," it said.
It said although Moroccan and Tunisian import requirements were seen lower, the expected rise in Egyptian and Algerian imports would help pare the drop in the region's overall needs.
The HGCA said the expected sharp increase in North African grain harvest this season would be led by Morocco. Algerian and Tunisian production are also estimated to be higher.
North Africa's wheat harvest is estimated 75 percent larger than last season and barley output nearly four times as large, it said.
The EU has been the favoured source of imports, with France supplying most of the EU wheat shipped to North Africa using credit facilities.
